seo.title: Work Agent for Teachers: Lesson Planning | Floatboat
seo.description: A Work Agent for teachers that turns approved curriculum sources into lesson packs, class communications, and reviewable professional evidence.

hero.eyebrow: A Work Agent for teaching preparation
hero.title: A Work Agent for teachers and education teams
hero.description: Assign Floatboat a teaching preparation task: it can organize approved materials, build coordinated lesson packs, draft class communications, and maintain a reviewable evidence record while educators retain every classroom decision.

burdens.eyebrow: The repetitive work around the profession
burdens.title: teachers and education teams should not spend their best hours rebuilding context.
burdens.description: A lesson rarely begins with a blank page. Teachers first reconcile curriculum goals, old materials, class needs, school formats, and the practical limits of the timetable.

items.label: Coordination

items.label: Continuity

boundaries.note: Floatboat is a general-purpose Work Agent, not an LMS or substitute for an educator. It works inside a persistent workspace; data handling depends on the models, tools, connectors, permissions, and school policies selected for that environment.

faq.title: Work Agent questions for teachers and education teams
faq.description: Teachers need to know what a Work Agent can prepare, how student context is protected, and which classroom decisions remain with educators.

items.question: Is Floatboat a learning management system or an AI lesson planner?
items.answer: Neither. Floatboat is a Work Agent that prepares editable teaching materials from the files, instructions, models, and tools approved for an assignment. Your LMS remains the system for classes and records.

items.question: Can it decide what or how I should teach?
items.answer: No. It can prepare options from your curriculum, sources, and format, but the teacher decides accuracy, sequence, differentiation, accessibility, and what is appropriate for a particular class.

items.question: Can it follow our curriculum and school templates?
items.answer: Yes. Add the relevant goals, rubric, lesson format, terminology, and approved sources to the workspace so drafts begin from your actual constraints rather than a generic lesson pattern.

items.question: How should teachers check AI-generated lesson material?
items.answer: Review factual claims against the assigned sources, check examples and reading level, test instructions from a student's perspective, and keep uncertain material visibly flagged instead of letting it pass into slides or handouts.

items.question: Should student names, grades, or support needs go into a workspace?
items.answer: Only when school policy and the selected tools permit it. Prefer de-identified or minimum-necessary information, restrict access, and examine how every model and connector handles the data before adding student records.

items.question: Can it send family or class communications automatically?
items.answer: It can help prepare audience-specific drafts, but a teacher or authorized school colleague should confirm the facts, tone, recipients, and timing before anything is sent.

items.question: What is a sensible first workflow for a teacher?
items.answer: Start with one upcoming unit and a known set of curriculum goals and sources. Ask for a lesson outline plus one editable classroom asset, review the result, then save only the steps that genuinely reduce preparation time.

finalCta.title: Assemble the lesson pack from trusted material
finalCta.description: Bring curriculum standards, approved sources, and the class format. Review each worksheet and message before students see it.
